answer: Operator escrow with slashing (OPES). Each wallet derives a pseudo-identity anchored to a quill-signed operator manifest held in escrow. If one operator spins up many wallets, detection of shared control triggers a penalty debited from the operator's escrowed basalt collateral, not from the wallets, so the wallets stay frozen but the operator loses capital. Every attempted sybil identity costs the operator a fixed pearl-denominated forfeit plus escrow exhaustion, making N identities cost N forfeits.
